Subject: P1: sudden throughput drop + 500s - ClarityAI-prod

We're seeing a sharp throughput drop across our prod endpoints starting ~08:45 PDT and a simultaneous spike in 500s (app-level) for about 30% of requests. Latency P95 jumped from ~120ms to >1.5s. This is customer-impacting (several live customers reporting timeouts). Our telemetry shows a correlated increase in KV cache evictions and an abnormal number of small retried batches. Attaching a screenshot of Grafana and a short excerpt from our logs.

Can you triage urgently and tell us: 1) is this on Redwood's side? 2) ETA to stabilize? 3) any temporary fallback (route to a different model/pool)?

On Fri, Aug 4, 2028 at 09:12 AM Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@clarityai.com> wrote:
> We're seeing a sharp throughput drop ... correlated increase in KV cache evictions ...

Thanks — quick summary of triage (first 20 minutes):
- Observed: simultaneous eviction storm on 3 KV shards that serve high-prefix churn for ClarityAI. Eviction rate increased 12x vs baseline.
- Root immediate effect: eviction-induced cache miss amplification + aggressive prefetch requests => batch worker lanes starved waiting for KV hits when prefetches thrash the cache. This creates head-of-line (HOL) blocking inside the serving queue; small batches pile up and worker slots are tied to long KV fetch waits, leading to CPU queueing and increased 500s when timeouts hit.
- Likely cause: a tenant-side traffic pattern change (spike in short-lived prefixes + prefetch enabled) combined with an aggressive eviction threshold we recently rolled to improve memory reuse on those shards.

Immediate mitigation plan (we can execute now; ETA in parentheses):
1) Reduce prefetch window and disable speculative prefix prefetch for ClarityAI tenant (10–15m) — low risk.
2) Apply temporary per-tenant eviction cap on suspect shards to limit churn (15–30m) — requires config push and soft restart on 3 nodes.
3) Route ClarityAI traffic to warmed dedicated pool with smaller batch sizes and +2 small-batch worker lanes (30–45m) — will reduce HOL visibility.
4) If still degraded, fall back to a compatible model variant with lower KV dependency for short-term (45–60m).

I've attached diagnostic logs and a config diff showing the eviction threshold change: diagnostics_20280804.log, kv-config-diff.txt.

Impact estimate: mitigations 1+2 typically cut eviction amplification within ~20m and reduce 500s noticeably in the next 30–60 minutes. Full stabilization and monitoring 2–4 hours.

I'll start with step 1 and 2 now and update as we progress.

Attachments: diagnostics_20280804.log, kv-config-diff.txt

—Marissa

Subject: Status: mitigations applied & initial recovery metrics

Hi all — final status update post-mitigations:
- Actions taken (completed Aug 04 10:05–10:40 PDT):
  * Disabled speculative prefix prefetch for ClarityAI tenant on affected shards.
  * Applied a per-tenant eviction cap on the three hot shards.
  * Moved traffic to a warmed dedicated pool with reduced batch sizes and +2 small-batch workers.
- Immediate results: eviction rate dropped ~85% in 20 minutes, P95 latency returned to ~140ms within 35 minutes, 500s rate back to baseline within 45 minutes.
- Attachments: runbook_temp_mitigations.md (short playbook we executed).

Next steps (ownership):
- SRE/Serving (Marissa): full RCA and prevention checklist (ETA 72 hours). We'll propose auto-detection rules for eviction storms and per-tenant prefetch caps as guardrails.
- Account (Aditya/Laura): confirm credit numbers and customer communication.
- Product (Ben): evaluate longer-term kernel-level protections to avoid HOL propagation under eviction amplification.

We'll keep monitoring ClarityAI for 48 hours and will post the RCA link to the HubSpot record and JIRA INF-4382.

—Marissa
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime
